subject: general
question: In May 2025, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) released the Human Development Index (HDI) 2024 report. What was India's rank on the HDI list?
solution:
The correct answer is __**134th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Human Development Report (HDR) 2023/24** released by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**, **India** secured the **134th** rank among **193 countries**. This reflects a slight improvement in its **Human Development Index (HDI)** value. ***Hence, the correct option is 134th.***
 
• **India's HDI value** increased to **0.644** in **2022**, up from **0.633** in **2021**. This score places India in the **'Medium Human Development'** category, showing progress after a brief decline during the **COVID-19 pandemic** years.
 
• The **2023/24 report** is titled **"Breaking the Gridlock: Reimagining Cooperation in a Polarized World."** It highlights that while global **HDI** reached a record high in **2023**, the gap between the richest and poorest nations is widening due to political **polarization** and **geopolitical tensions**.
 
• The report notes significant improvements in **India's** performance across all key indicators, including **life expectancy**, **education**, and **Gross National Income (GNI)** per capita, which contributed to the rise in its global standing compared to the previous **135th** rank.
 
• In the regional context, **India** ranks higher than some of its neighbors like **Pakistan (164th)** and **Myanmar (144th)**, but remains behind **Sri Lanka (78th)** and **China (75th)** in the human development hierarchy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dimensions of HDI**: The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a composite index that measures average achievement in **three basic dimensions** of human development:

 
 
• **A long and healthy life**: Measured by **Life Expectancy at Birth**. In India, this increased from **62.7 years** to **67.7 years** according to recent data.
 
• **Knowledge**: Measured by **Mean Years of Schooling** (for adults aged **25 years** and older) and **Expected Years of Schooling** (for children of school entering age). India’s **expected years of schooling** stood at **12.6 years**.
 
• **A decent standard of living**: Measured by **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita** based on **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)**. India’s **GNI per capita** increased to **$6,951**.
 
 
 
• **Gender Inequality Index (GII)**: In the same report, **India** stood at the **108th** rank out of **193 countries** with a score of **0.437**. This index measures gender inequalities in **reproductive health**, **empowerment**, and **labor market participation**.
 
• **Global Rankings**: In the **2023/24** report, **Switzerland** maintained its position at **rank 1**, followed by **Norway** and **Iceland**. These countries are categorized under **'Very High Human Development'**.
 
• **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**: It was established in **1965** by the **United Nations General Assembly**. Headquartered in **New York City**, it is the **UN's** global development network, focusing on poverty reduction, **HIV/AIDS**, democratic governance, and **environmental sustainability**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **HDI** was created by Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and Indian economist **Amartya Sen** in **1990** to emphasize that people and their capabilities should be the ultimate criteria for assessing the development of a country.
 
• The index ranges from **0 to 1**. A value closer to **1** indicates a higher level of human development. India's shift to **0.644** reflects a steady upward trajectory since **1990**, when its value was approximately **0.434**.
 
• **Government Initiatives**: India’s improvement is often attributed to large-scale missions such as **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** (sanitation), **Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana** (clean energy), and **Ayushman Bharat** (health insurance), which directly impact the **HDI** components.
